hook_text: Half a pizza or four eighths of a pizza? Which would you rather have?
clip_script: Supper in Kimberley. One pizza, cut in half. Mom takes one half. Now cut every slice in two: four slices, Mom has two of them, two quarters. Cut again: eight slices, Mom has four, four eighths. Did Mom get more pizza? No! Same pizza, more cuts. One half equals two quarters equals four eighths. The rule: times the top and the bottom by the same number. Three quarters into eighths? Times 2 and times 2: six eighths. And the trap: add 1 to top and bottom of one half and you get two thirds, which is more pizza from nowhere. Multiply, never add.
visual_style: Whiteboard pizza being cut again and again with Mom's share outlined; a fraction wall with a vertical line through 1/2, 2/4 and 4/8.
pacing: The pizza question, two rounds of cutting, the rule, then the adding trap.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and fold a paper strip to find three names for one half.
